job.title: Desktop Home Assessor - Insurer with amazing growth and opportunity!
job.description:
We are currently recruiting for Desktop Home Assessors on behalf of one of Australia’s leading insurance providers. This organisation is behind several well-known insurance brands, operates nationally, and offers excellent career development opportunities, structured training programs, and clear career pathways.

This is an exciting opportunity to utilise your construction, trades, building, or estimating experience in an office-based role as a Desktop Home Assessor within the Home Claims team.

What's in It for You?

This is an opportunity to join a fast-growing insurance organisation in an office-based role with a supportive, team-focused culture and strong career development opportunities.
  • Comprehensive training and clear career progression pathways.
  • Full-time permanent salary of between $80,000-$100,000 inclusive of Super.
  • Volunteer leave, an additional paid "ME" day, paid parental leave, and the option to purchase extra annual leave.
  • Discounts on insurance products and selected retail offers.
  • A social and supportive team environment with regular events and activities.
  • An office-based opportunity working Monday-Friday across general business hours.
What would the Role Entail?

This role is ideal for someone with strong building and construction experience who is looking to transition their hands-on experience into a stable, office-based position while remaining closely connected to the industry. We are particularly keen to hear from candidates with experience working for insurance builders, particularly those with exposure to insurance repairs, estimating, scopes of work, claims or repair coordination.

As a Desktop Home Assessor, you will manage home insurance claims from assessment through to completion. Using your building and construction knowledge, you will review claim information, assess property damage, determine the required scope of works, and prepare repair and restoration cost estimates.

Working closely with customers, repairers, builders, and internal stakeholders, you will ensure claims are managed efficiently, repair solutions are practical and cost-effective, and customers are supported throughout the process.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Reviewing claim documentation, photographs, reports, and quotations to assess property damage.
  • Determining repair scopes and preparing accurate cost estimates.
  • Negotiating repair costs and outcomes with builders and repair partners.
  • Managing claims through to completion, ensuring timelines and budgets are met.
  • Providing recommendations regarding repairs, cash settlements, and temporary accommodation requirements.
  • Liaising with customers and stakeholders to provide updates and manage expectations.
  
What Skills Do I Need?

To be successful in this position, you will have:
  • Experience within the building, construction, trades, or estimating sectors, with the comfortability to apply your technical knowledge to property claims.
  • Experience reviewing and preparing accurate scopes of work.
  • A willingness to learn and develop within the insurance industry through a structured training program.
  • Strong organisational skills and a high level of attention to detail.
  • The ability to manage both phone-based and administrative tasks while building relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

If you have the skills required and are interested in proceeding with the opportunity, please click 'Apply' or if you have any questions please email/call Emma @ SMAART Recruitment on emmas@smaart.com.au/0432244813

We're looking for someone with strong contact centre leadership experience, ideally within outbound sales, fundraising, retention, acquisition or another target-driven environment.
Fundraising experience would be advantageous but isn't essential. More important is your ability to lead a diverse team, understand performance drivers and get involved when needed.

  • Previous contact centre management experience
  • Experience leading managers, team leaders and frontline teams
  • Exposure to outbound sales or KPI-driven environments
  • A practical, hands-on leadership style
  • Strong coaching and people-development skills
  • Confidence interpreting operational data and reporting
  • Experience with CRM and dialler platforms
  • Strong planning and commercial awareness
  • The ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment
The Environment:
This is not a traditional corporate contact centre. The team is diverse, energetic and full of personality, with hands-on senior leaders and long-standing client relationships.
There is plenty happening at once, so you'll need to be adaptable, comfortable making decisions and ready to get involved. You'll also have the opportunity to bring fresh ideas and take real ownership of the operation as it grows.

Your portfolio will predominantly cover landlord policies, contents, tenant damage and tenant default claims, with limited building claims. You will typically manage around 100 active claims, working closely with property managers, landlords, tenants and external service providers.

You will assess: policy coverage, liability and quantum within your delegated authority, investigate claims, maintain accurate documentation and proactively manage each claim through to resolution. Just as importantly, you will be the key point of contact for your customers and stakeholders, keeping them informed and clearly explaining decisions throughout the claims process.

About You:
We are looking for someone with at least 1-2 years' experience within domestic property claims or a closely related insurance environment. Experience across landlord, residential property, contents or strata claims would be particularly relevant.

You will be comfortable managing your own portfolio, confident making decisions within delegated authority and able to balance customer outcomes with policy, compliance and commercial considerations.

Strong communication, organisation and time management skills are important, but attitude and aptitude are equally valued. You will be someone who takes ownership, enjoys being part of a team and genuinely wants to continue developing their career within insurance.

  • One-on-one training and buddying as you settle into the role
